  <Revision version="20.6.10" priority="Critical">
   Owner-approved method change (owner question 30, 2026-10-03): product reviews as community evidence. For a product
   or service people buy, map where its buyers review it before sampling (PrincipalPlatformMapping); keep the exact
   product and its ingredient as separate cohorts, checked against the label (ScopeAxesBeforeSampling); search review
   text in every direction and language (DirectionalSearchSymmetry); treat top-ranked, outcome-word, snippet, and
   summary reviews as discovery, recording how many reviews were shown and read and how they were chosen
   (ReviewCorpusSelectionAndCounts); count a review once across listings, variants, and retailers
   (UniqueFirsthandUnit); label review sources and incentives (CommercialAndCommunityBias); keep a carer's observation
   of a dependent in its own cohort (NoForumSignalByProxy, CaregiverObservedCohort); and record an unreachable review
   corpus as partial or inaccessible (ClosedPlatformAndAccessDisclosure). Two stress cases and final checks FS210 and
   FS211.
  </Revision>

  <Rule name="ReviewCorpusSelectionAndCounts" priority="Critical">
   On a review platform, top-ranked reviews, reviews found by outcome words, snippets, and summaries (such as a
   platform's generated “customers say” text) are discovery: they show which experiences exist, not how common each
   is. For each product and platform, record how many written reviews the platform shows, how many were retrieved and
   analyzed, and how they were selected. Label direction only within a frame not chosen by outcome: every review,
   every review mentioning the condition, the most recent reviews, a random sample, or a rating-stratified sample
   weighted by the platform's rating counts (DirectionLabelsNeedOutcomeNeutralSelection). From any other set, report
   the directions observed with their frequency unknown. Star ratings are not outcome reports: they also rate taste,
   price, delivery, and packaging. One review shows that an experience exists, never how often it occurs.
  </Rule>

periods or documented rechallenges are analytically relevant.

periods or documented rechallenges are analytically relevant.
   A review shown on several listings, sizes, flavors, bundles, or retailers counts once. Match reviews by text, date,
   and the platform's review identifiers; use reviewer names, handles, and identifiers only for that matching, and
   never report or save them.
  </Rule>

  <Rule name="CaregiverObservedCohort" priority="Critical">
   A parent's or carer's report of what they directly observed in a child or dependent who used the intervention is
   neither a firsthand report nor discarded hearsay. Keep these reports in a separately labeled caregiver-observed
   cohort, never pooled with self-reports. Observable outcomes, such as behavior, sleep, school or work reports,
   measured values, and adverse reactions, carry weight there; the dependent's inner experiences, such as mood, focus,
   or craving, stay weaker proxy evidence. Apply the same direction, deduplication, and selection rules as to
   self-reports.
  </Rule>

treatment enthusiasm, reputational stakes, platform recommendation systems, and coordinated or duplicated language.

treatment enthusiasm, reputational stakes, platform recommendation systems, and coordinated or duplicated language.

   review, not whether its outcome report is accurate.

  <Case id="ProductReviewCorpusForSupplementQuestion">
   <Prompt>
    Does a humic acid supplement help children with ADHD? Two Reddit threads mention it; one brand's drops have 2,400
    reviews on a large retailer, whose first page shows eight favorable top-ranked reviews.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Map the retailer's reviews as a principal community, and do not call the signal absent from Reddit alone. Search
    the exact product and humic acid separately and check the label. Search the review text in every direction with
    words such as ADHD, focus, attention, hyperactivity, behavior, sleep, no difference, worse, and stopped. Treat the
    eight top-ranked reviews as discovery with each direction's frequency unknown; record the 2,400 shown and how many
    were read and how they were chosen; count a review repeated across sizes or listings once; and if the full set
    cannot be reached, record that corpus as partial or inaccessible.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="ParentReviewOfChildOutcome">
   <Prompt>
    A review of the same drops reads: "My son has ADHD. After a month his teacher says he finishes his work, and he
    sleeps better." Is it a firsthand report?
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Place it in the caregiver-observed cohort, apart from self-reports. Count the teacher's report and the sleep
    change as observed outcomes, treat any claim about how the child feels as weaker proxy evidence, and do not discard
    it as secondhand.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
</StressTestExpectations>
